title: Vaginal bleeding in pregnancy
summary: Any bleeding from the genital tract in pregnancy, before onset of labour.
redFlags: Signs of shock or collapse (faint/dizzy, racing heart, clammy, confused) — this is an emergency regardless of visible blood loss.
Severe or worsening one-sided abdominal pain, or pain out of proportion to bleeding — think ectopic.
Constant severe pain, a tense/'woody' hard uterus, or bleeding that seems less than the degree of shock would suggest — think concealed placental abruption.
Known low-lying placenta / placenta praevia with any bleeding.

blocks.heading: Signs of shock or collapse
bullets: Call 999 / put out an emergency call per local major obstetric haemorrhage protocol — do not drive her in yourself.
Do not perform a digital vaginal examination — placenta praevia has not been excluded.
Prepare for emergency transfer/resuscitation: IV access, bloods including group & save/crossmatch, senior obstetric and anaesthetic input.
See the Major obstetric haemorrhage emergency drill for full actions.

blocks.heading: Suspected ectopic pregnancy (under 24 weeks)
bullets: Severe or worsening one-sided pain, shoulder-tip pain, or pain out of proportion to bleeding.
Arrange emergency transfer for assessment — do not wait for a routine early pregnancy unit slot.
Early pregnancy unit or gynaecology emergency assessment with urgent ultrasound and beta-hCG.
Call 999 immediately if any signs of shock/collapse develop at any point.

blocks.heading: Suspected placental abruption (24+ weeks)
bullets: Constant severe pain, tense/'woody' hard uterus, or bleeding that seems less than the degree of pain/shock would suggest (can be concealed).
Call 999 / emergency obstetric response per local major obstetric haemorrhage / abruption protocol.
Continuous fetal monitoring as soon as available; anticipate fetal compromise.
IV access, bloods including group & save/crossmatch and clotting, senior obstetric and anaesthetic input.
Do not perform a digital vaginal examination until placenta praevia excluded.

blocks.heading: Known low-lying placenta / praevia (24+ weeks)
bullets: Admit for assessment — do NOT perform a digital vaginal examination.
Continuous or intermittent fetal monitoring as clinically indicated; maternal observations.
Urgent obstetric review; ultrasound to reassess placental position/bleeding source if not recently done.
Group & save/crossmatch per local major obstetric haemorrhage protocol given known praevia.

blocks.heading: Early-pregnancy bleeding (under 24 weeks), no red flags
bullets: Heavier bleeding or passing clots/tissue: arrange same-day early pregnancy unit (or emergency gynaecology if EPU closed) assessment with ultrasound.
Fever, offensive discharge, or an open cervix on examination: same-day assessment and consider sepsis screen (see Sepsis emergency drill if she appears unwell).
Light spotting/period-like with no other concerns: routine early pregnancy unit referral; advise rest and avoiding intercourse/tampons until reviewed — VERIFY local advice wording.

blocks.heading: Antepartum bleeding (24+ weeks), no red flags and praevia not known
bullets: Heavier bleeding (soaking pads, clots): admit for assessment, do not perform digital vaginal examination until placenta praevia excluded by scan/notes; continuous fetal monitoring (CTG), group & save/crossmatch, urgent obstetric review, ultrasound.

Spotting/light with contractions, reduced fetal movements, or other concerns: admit for assessment, CTG and maternal observations, urgent obstetric review to assess for labour, abruption, or other cause.
Spotting/light with no other concerns: same-day assessment, CTG, maternal observations, obstetric review; speculum examination once praevia excluded, to look for a local cause if appropriate.

blocks.heading: Safety-netting to give
bullets: Call 999 or attend A&E immediately if bleeding becomes heavier/heavy, pain develops or worsens (especially one-sided), or she feels faint, dizzy, or unwell.
Come back at any time, however many times, if still worried.

blocks.heading: What to document
bullets: Estimated blood loss and duration; pain characteristics.
Placental position if known; gestation.
CTG/fetal heart findings once available.
Route of referral and time; plan and review time.
